$comment: Scheme-agency profile. The single source of truth for the UBL @schemeAgencyID attribute on party/reference cbc:ID elements (cac:PartyIdentification/cbc:ID, cbc:ContractFolderID, cac:AgentParty/cbc:ID). @schemeAgencyID names the agency that MAINTAINS the identification scheme the id belongs to; BR-OTH-02 (fatal) makes it mandatory and non-empty on every cbc:ID. It is NOT a user-entered field in this implementation: it is DERIVED at export. A mapping rule references a profile here via { fromMap: { path?, profile } } — `path` (rule-specific) names the instance field whose value is looked up in `map`; when there is no `path` (or the value is unmapped), the profile `default` applies. Resolution happens once at spec-load time (model/mapping-engine/resolve-scheme-agency.mjs), so the mapping engine itself stays data-only. Change the policy HERE, in one place; the four identifier mappings (partI/sectionB, partI/sectionC, partII/sectionA, partII/sectionB) all reference it.

identifier-scheme-agency.$comment: Agency per identifier scheme (EOIDType.gc codes), with a safe default. VAT→VIES matches ESPD-Request-BASE.xml (the EU VAT Information Exchange System). LEI→GLEIF is the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation, the authoritative LEI registry. DUNS→D&B is Dun & Bradstreet, which issues D-U-N-S numbers. BRIS (the EU Business Registers Interconnection System) and NATIONAL (whichever national register, country-dependent) have no single short agency token, so they take the default. The default OP (Publications Office of the European Union) is also used for identifiers that carry NO scheme field to derive from — the buyer's own file reference (cbc:ContractFolderID) and the Part II economic-operator / agent identifiers (the Response model carries no @schemeID on them). OP is the agency used uniformly for the codelist-backed ids across the whole document, so it keeps @schemeAgencyID consistent and BR-OTH-02-valid.
